name: Vidago Palace Hotel
positioning: Palace hotel from 1910 in the heart of the Vidago Thermal Park in northern Portugal, with a spa, Club House and golf course
best_for: Travelers who want a historic palace stay with spa and golf
Guests who enjoy strolling a historic park setting

facts.text: The hotel is housed in a century-old palace in the heart of the Vidago Thermal Park, surrounded by mountains and forest.
The palace was initially known for its thermal baths.
The interior design is by Portuguese architects José Pedro Lopes Vieira and Diogo Rosa Lã.
The historic city of Chaves is 15 minutes from the hotel.
The park's groves, paths, trails and water mirrors invite strolls through trees that change colour with the seasons.
Hotel venues include the restaurant Salão Nobre, the Jardim de Inverno, a bar, a pool bar and a wine shop.
The hotel has a Kids Club.
Pets may walk in the hotel's park on a leash.
A portion of the park access proceeds goes to the Vidago Volunteer Fire Department.

highlights.text: The Vidago Palace Hotel was inaugurated on 6 October 1910, the year the First Portuguese Republic was established.
In the 19th century, King D. Carlos I wished to see a luxury therapeutic spa built in Vidago with international projection.
The hotel's golf course was designed by architect Philip Mackenzie Ross.
The Spa and Club House were designed by architect Álvaro Siza Vieira.
Guided tours of the hotel's interior include a brief historical presentation and a water tasting directly from the source, subject to availability and prior booking.

considerations.text: The hotel is about one hour from Porto.
Vidago Park also admits outside visitors, who pay an entry fee; hotel guests have free access.
WhataHotel notes limited dining and entertainment options in the surrounding area.
